items.title: Telangana govt asks Karnataka to release water as Jurala reservoir faces stress
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. With standing crops in the Palamuru region facing water stress amid limited inflows into the Jurala reservoir, the Telangana government has stepped up efforts to secure additional water from Karnataka’s Upper Krishna system. Telangana Irrigation Minister N Uttam Kumar Reddy said Telangana had approached Karnataka Chief Minister DK Shivakumar with a request to release water from the Narayanpur reservoir. Such a release, he said, could augment inflows into Jurala and provide immediate relief to farmers dependent on the irrigation project. A delegation comprising Animal Husbandry Minister Vakiti Srihari, Excise and Tourism Minister Jupally Krishna Rao and MLAs Bandla Krishna Mohan Reddy, Madhusudhan Reddy and Megha Reddy travelled to Bengaluru to pursue the request with the Karnataka government. Uttam Kumar said the request had been made against the backdrop of difficult conditions in the Krishna basin and the pressing requirement to protect standing crops in the erstwhile Mahabubnagar district.
